title: The first transistor used two contacts on a sliver of germanium
body: In 1947 John Bardeen and Walter Brattain demonstrated a semiconductor amplifier at Bell Labs. Their point-contact transistor used two metal contacts touching a small piece of germanium.
takeaway: The device showed that a solid semiconductor could amplify a signal, work previously done by vacuum tubes.
source: Computer History Museum, Invention of the Point-Contact Transistor (1947)
visual: two fine metal contacts touching a tiny piece of germanium on a laboratory bench

title: A daguerreotype is a photograph with no original negative
body: Announced in 1839, Louis Daguerre's process made an image directly on a silver-coated copper plate. Each plate was a unique photograph, without a separate negative for printing duplicates.
takeaway: Copies needed another act of photography, rather than another print from the same negative.
source: Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Photograph of Louis Daguerre
visual: a reflective photographic plate inside the open case of an early camera
